children: The following are expectations for the resumption of grain and soy complex trading at the Chicago Board of Trade at 8:30 a.m. CDT (1330 GMT) on Wednesday.
WHEAT - Down 1 to 3 cents per bushel
CBOT wheat
turned lower in choppy trading on Wednesday as the market weighed diplomatic efforts to end Russia's war with Ukraine against continued disruption to Black Sea exports.

Ukraine struck targets at Novorossiysk, including a naval base and a terminal for loading oil, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said. Traders cited unconfirmed talk that grain infrastructure at the port had also been damaged.
Comments by the Kremlin saying that Russia hopes U.S.-mediated talks will resume soon and that it sees Abu Dhabi as a preferred venue for such talks, put the focus back on diplomatic efforts.
Sovecon lowered its Russian grain export forecast on Wednesday due to increasing disruption to the Azov-Black Sea canal.

CBOT December soft red winter wheat (WZ26) was last 1/2 cent lower to 7.46-1/2 per bushel. K.C. December hard red winter wheat (KWZ26) was last 1-1/2 cents lower to $8.17-1/2 a bushel. Minneapolis December spring wheat (MWEZ26) was last 1/2 cent higher to $7.55-1/2 a bushel.
CORN - Down 3 to 4 cents per bushel
CBOT corn
eased, with attention turning towards U.S. Department of Agriculture forecasts on Friday that will offer a gauge of weather damage to Midwest crops.
The USDA's supply-and-demand forecasts are awaited as an indicator of the extent to which hot, dry spells this summer hurt U.S. Midwest crops.
On Tuesday, the USDA estimated that 56% of the corn crop was in good-to-excellent condition, down 1 percentage point from the previous week but in line with average analyst expectations.
CBOT December corn (CZ26) was last down 2-3/4 cents to $5.29-3/4 per bushel.
SOYBEANS - Down 1 to 3 cents per bushel
CBOT soybeans
fell in positioning ahead of Friday's USDA report.
The good/excellent score for soybeans was unchanged at 58%, exceeding average expectations of a 1 point fall.
A rally in oil prices, with Brent futures on Wednesday surpassing $100 a barrel for the first time since July, has also lent support to corn and soybeans that are widely used for producing biofuel.
CBOT November soybeans (SX26) were last down 2-3/4 cents to $13.13-1/2 per bushel.
